result:
Solution 1 gives no derivation. Its answer √5 is below the value 2.66 that the extremal polynomial in Solutions 2 and 3 attains, and nothing in Solution 1 supports it. I reject it.

Solutions 2 and 3 use f(z) = z³ − z² + z + 1. On the unit circle |f(e^{iθ})|² = 4 − 2cosθ + 2cos3θ. With x = cosθ this equals 4 + 8x³ − 8x. Its maximum on [−1, 1] is at x = −1/√3, where the value is 4 + 16√3/9. So M² = (36 + 16√3)/9, which gives M ≈ 2.66. The two final expressions, 2√(9+4√3)/3 and √(36+16√3)/3, are equal.

I did not prove that no other choice of coefficients does better. The case A₂ = 0 reduces to a one-parameter family in which a phase of π is the optimum. A spot check of the phase π/2 gave a larger maximum. The perturbation arguments for A₂ ≠ 0 in Solutions 2 and 3 are not rigorous. I recall this value as the known answer, so I accept both.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
